label: m:E001
prompt:
You are performing a blinded radiological image-reading task. You have NO access to any ground truth or label. Do NOT read any CSV, JSON, or other project file — use ONLY the images described. Base your answer solely on what you visually observe.

Open and visually examine ALL 63 axial slice images (CONTIGUOUS, caudal -> cranial through the heart — no slices are skipped) in this directory:
C:\Users\Usuario\Documents\Investigacion\Articulos originales\CAC_confirm_reader_package\images\full\E001\
named slice_000.png, slice_001.png, ... through slice_062.png (zero-padded THREE digits, 63 files total). Read every one of them.

TASK INSTRUCTIONS:

You are evaluating axial slices from a NON-CONTRAST low-dose chest CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening. No intravenous contrast. Standard mediastinal window (WW=350/WL=40).

KEY IMAGING FACT: On this NON-CONTRAST scan, blood and non-calcified vessel walls appear GRAY. Any sharply BRIGHT/WHITE structure (as bright as bone) within the heart or along the coronary course represents CALCIUM. Do not dismiss bright intracardiac foci as contrast/vessels. Equally, do not invent calcium where the heart is uniformly gray.

CAC = calcium in the walls of LM, LAD (anterior interventricular groove), LCx (left AV groove), RCA (right AV groove); LM/proximal LAD/LCx near the aortic root. CAC is NOT aortic valve/mitral/pericardial/thoracic-aorta-wall/pulmonary-vessel/granuloma/bone/costal-cartilage calcium (list under alternative_findings).

HOW TO SCORE:
Step 1. Examine each coronary (LM, LAD, LCx, RCA) across the series; note absent / isolated flecks / dense-continuous, and on how many slices. Because the slices are contiguous, a calcified vessel will appear on several consecutive slices — follow it.
Step 2. Count vessels involved (N).
Step 3. Integrate the WHOLE series (CAC-DRS visual ordinal):
  - NONE -> "0": no coronary calcium.
  - MILD -> "1-100": isolated flecks (small, sparse, one vessel, few slices).
  - MODERATE -> "101-300": more than flecks; 1-2 vessels with definite calcium over several slices.
  - SEVERE -> ">300": continuous/dense deposits, extensive, often multiple vessels, many slices.

CALIBRATION: Do not anchor on a single focus. Dense, continuous, or multi-vessel calcium over several slices is SEVERE (>300), not mild. Isolated faint specks are MILD (not NONE). Bone/cartilage/aortic-wall calcium is not CAC.

Return your assessment as the structured object.

Reading-harness requirement (not part of the clinical instructions): before answering, open every one of the 63 files above with the Read tool; you may issue many Read calls in a single turn. Do not open any other file or directory and do not use any other tool.

You are performing a blinded radiological image-reading task. You have NO access to any ground truth or label. Do NOT read any CSV, JSON, or other project file — use ONLY the images described. Base your answer solely on what you visually observe.

Open and visually examine ALL 68 axial slice images (CONTIGUOUS, caudal -> cranial through the heart — no slices are skipped) in this directory:
C:\Users\Usuario\Documents\Investigacion\Articulos originales\CAC_confirm_reader_package\images\full\E088\
named slice_000.png, slice_001.png, ... through slice_067.png (zero-padded THREE digits, 68 files total). Read every one of them.

TASK INSTRUCTIONS:

You are evaluating axial slices from a NON-CONTRAST low-dose chest CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening. No intravenous contrast. Standard mediastinal window (WW=350/WL=40).

KEY IMAGING FACT: On this NON-CONTRAST scan, blood and non-calcified vessel walls appear GRAY. Any sharply BRIGHT/WHITE structure (as bright as bone) within the heart or along the coronary course represents CALCIUM. Do not dismiss bright intracardiac foci as contrast/vessels. Equally, do not invent calcium where the heart is uniformly gray.

CAC = calcium in the walls of LM, LAD (anterior interventricular groove), LCx (left AV groove), RCA (right AV groove); LM/proximal LAD/LCx near the aortic root. CAC is NOT aortic valve/mitral/pericardial/thoracic-aorta-wall/pulmonary-vessel/granuloma/bone/costal-cartilage calcium (list under alternative_findings).

HOW TO SCORE:
Step 1. Examine each coronary (LM, LAD, LCx, RCA) across the series; note absent / isolated flecks / dense-continuous, and on how many slices. Because the slices are contiguous, a calcified vessel will appear on several consecutive slices — follow it.
Step 2. Count vessels involved (N).
Step 3. Integrate the WHOLE series (CAC-DRS visual ordinal):
  - NONE -> "0": no coronary calcium.
  - MILD -> "1-100": isolated flecks (small, sparse, one vessel, few slices).
  - MODERATE -> "101-300": more than flecks; 1-2 vessels with definite calcium over several slices.
  - SEVERE -> ">300": continuous/dense deposits, extensive, often multiple vessels, many slices.

CALIBRATION: Do not anchor on a single focus. Dense, continuous, or multi-vessel calcium over several slices is SEVERE (>300), not mild. Isolated faint specks are MILD (not NONE). Bone/cartilage/aortic-wall calcium is not CAC.

Return your assessment as the structured object.

Open and visually examine ALL 81 axial slice images (CONTIGUOUS, caudal -> cranial through the heart — no slices are skipped) in this directory:
C:\Users\Usuario\Documents\Investigacion\Articulos originales\CAC_confirm_reader_package\images\full\E072\
named slice_000.png, slice_001.png, ... through slice_080.png (zero-padded THREE digits, 81 files total). Read every one of them.

TASK INSTRUCTIONS:

You are evaluating axial slices from a NON-CONTRAST low-dose chest CT (LDCT) for lung cancer screening. No intravenous contrast. Standard mediastinal window (WW=350/WL=40).

KEY IMAGING FACT: On this NON-CONTRAST scan, blood and non-calcified vessel walls appear GRAY. Any sharply BRIGHT/WHITE structure (as bright as bone) within the heart or along the coronary course represents CALCIUM. Do not dismiss bright intracardiac foci as contrast/vessels. Equally, do not invent calcium where the heart is uniformly gray.

CAC = calcium in the walls of LM, LAD (anterior interventricular groove), LCx (left AV groove), RCA (right AV groove); LM/proximal LAD/LCx near the aortic root. CAC is NOT aortic valve/mitral/pericardial/thoracic-aorta-wall/pulmonary-vessel/granuloma/bone/costal-cartilage calcium (list under alternative_findings).

HOW TO SCORE:
Step 1. Examine each coronary (LM, LAD, LCx, RCA) across the series; note absent / isolated flecks / dense-continuous, and on how many slices. Because the slices are contiguous, a calcified vessel will appear on several consecutive slices — follow it.
Step 2. Count vessels involved (N).
Step 3. Integrate the WHOLE series (CAC-DRS visual ordinal):
  - NONE -> "0": no coronary calcium.
  - MILD -> "1-100": isolated flecks (small, sparse, one vessel, few slices).
  - MODERATE -> "101-300": more than flecks; 1-2 vessels with definite calcium over several slices.
  - SEVERE -> ">300": continuous/dense deposits, extensive, often multiple vessels, many slices.

CALIBRATION: Do not anchor on a single focus. Dense, continuous, or multi-vessel calcium over several slices is SEVERE (>300), not mild. Isolated faint specks are MILD (not NONE). Bone/cartilage/aortic-wall calcium is not CAC.

Return your assessment as the structured object.
